_about: Rule thresholds. Every entry has a basis: "sourced" (see its source key in `sources`) or "app default" (a Cosmic Shield setting, not a NASA standard or clinical cut-off). See docs/rules.md.

sources.nasa-std-3001-career: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 (NASA Space Flight Human-System Standard, Crew Health): universal career effective-dose limit of 600 mSv. Confirmed via Zanon C et al., Tomography 2026;12(7):106 (doi:10.3390/tomography12070106), which cites the NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief; NASA's own PDF links returned 404 when checked (2026-11-13).
sources.who-pulse-oximetry-2011: World Health Organization. Pulse Oximetry Training Manual. WHO Patient Safety, 2011 (ISBN 978 92 4 150113 2), https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/patient-safety/pulse-oximetry/who-ps-pulse-oxymetry-training-manual-en.pdf. Verbatim: "During anaesthesia the oxygen saturation should always be 95 - 100%. If the oxygen saturation is 94% or lower, the patient is hypoxic and needs to be treated quickly. A saturation of less than 90% is a clinical emergency." Written for anaesthesia providers; applied here as a general hypoxaemia cut-off.
sources.aha-bp-categories: American Heart Association. Understanding Blood Pressure Readings, https://goredforwomen.org/en/health-topics/high-blood-pressure/understanding-blood-pressure-readings (the AHA's own Go Red for Women mirror of heart.org/bplevels; heart.org and the mirror both return 403 to automated fetches, so the wording was read from the page by the project team, 2026-11-13). Verbatim: category "HYPERTENSIVE CRISIS (consult your doctor immediately)", values "HIGHER THAN 180 and/or HIGHER THAN 120"; guidance "Wait five minutes after your first reading." / "Take your blood pressure again." / "If your readings are still unusually high, contact your health care professional immediately."
sources.lewis-heaton-1997: Lewis SJ, Heaton KW. Stool form scale as a useful guide to intestinal transit time. Scand J Gastroenterol 1997;32(9):920–924. doi:10.3109/00365529709011203. Defines the seven stool types used here (type 1 separate hard lumps … type 7 watery, no solid pieces).
sources.nasa-iss-exercise-2024: NASA, "Astronaut Exercise" (Science in Space, May 20, 2024; page last updated Feb 3, 2025), https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/iss-research/astronaut-exercise/: "crew members now averaging two hours of exercise per day."
sources.nasa-nutrition-2021: Smith SM, Zwart SR, Douglas GL, Heer M. Human Adaptation to Spaceflight: The Role of Food and Nutrition, 2nd ed. NASA, 2021 (https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/human_adaptation_2021_final.pdf). Table 1 (Nutritional Requirements Defined for ISS and Exploration Missions): calcium, ISS (1996) 1,200–2,000 mg; exploration (2020) 1,000–1,200 mg. Vitamin D, ISS (1996) 10 µg; exploration (2005) 25 µg; exploration (2020) 1000 IU (25 µg). Text: in-flight 25-hydroxyvitamin D data "provide evidence that 800 IU vitamin D/d is enough to maintain vitamin D status during long-duration spaceflight".
sources.ada-hypoglycemia-levels-2025: American Diabetes Association. Guidelines InSIGHT: Hypoglycemia (Low Blood Glucose), patient version, based on the Standards of Care in Diabetes—2025, https://professional.diabetes.org/sites/dpro/files/2025-05/hypoglycemia-patient-5-27-25.pdf. Verbatim: "LEVEL 1 Your blood glucose is less than 70 mg/dL but over or at 54 mg/dL"; "LEVEL 2 Your blood glucose is less than 54 mg/dL".
sources.radlab-iss-altea: NASA OSDR RadLab, ISS ALTEA-Survey dose_equivalent_rate, 1–7 Jun 2011: 0.717 mSv/day (data/nasa/derived/radiation-environments.json).
sources.nasa-mars-factsheet: NASA Mars Fact Sheet (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/marsfact.html): Earth–Mars distance 54.6–401.4 × 10^6 km; maximum one-way light time = 401.4e6 km ÷ 299,792.458 km/s ≈ 22.3 min.

glucoseMgDl.note: watchHigh is an app default display band, not a diagnostic cut-off. Fasting status is not recorded with the reading.

bloodPressureEscalate.note: AHA 'Hypertensive crisis': higher than 180 and/or higher than 120 mmHg (strictly greater than). 180/120 itself is not Escalate.

radiationMsvDay.watchHighNote: 2 × the measured ISS daily dose, rounded to 0.1 (the same heuristic as each mission environment's Watch threshold).
radiationMsvDay.cumulativeWatchNote: Half of the 600 mSv career limit.

mind.note: Self-rated daily check-in, 1–5 scales. Watch only; never Escalate. Not a screening tool.

bone.note: The daily exercise target is the mission environment's: ISS 120 min is sourced (NASA, about two hours a day); the other environments and the 120 min used when none is chosen are app defaults. Calcium and vitamin D targets are sourced (NASA nutrition requirements). The bone_exercise rule itself (Watch below 50 % of the weekly target) is an app default. Watch only.
bone.calciumNote: Lower bound of NASA's 2020 exploration requirement (1,000–1,200 mg/day); the 1996 ISS requirement was 1,200–2,000 mg.
bone.vitaminDNote: In-flight data show 800 IU/day maintains vitamin D status; NASA's 2020 exploration requirement is 1000 IU/day.

gi.note: Bristol type meanings follow the Bristol Stool Form Scale (Lewis & Heaton 1997, source lewis-heaton-1997). The two pattern rules (2 or more of the last 3 UTC days with types 1–2, or with types 6–7) and the 2–3 L daily fluid band are app defaults with no verified source. Watch only; never a diagnosis.

gamification.note: Motivation only; never affects a health status. Only the first entry of each activity per UTC day earns points.
